messages:
sara: Heads-up — I reproduced the perf regression on the kv-attach path. Small batches (~4-8) show a kernel routing jump and higher tail latency. :eyes:
aj: ugh. which capture flags did you use?
sara: Quick nsys run, trying to keep it short so we don't blow up the qdrep: ```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --output=kv-attach.qdrep --capture-range=nvtx:kv_attach_start:kv_attach_end --duration=12 
```
devon: nice. two quick things: 1) sample window = 12s might miss short-lived kernel churn if warmup is long; 2) OSRT traces will show queue timelines vs kernel timelines — good for batching heuristics.
kevin: also check that the runtime isn't hitting the float16 kernel selection for seq<32 — that switches kernels and we saw a jump last week.
sara: saw that — nvtx markers show a large gap between enqueue and actual kernel start when batch<=8. attached an excerpt of nvtx timeline: ```
NVTX: enqueue_batch -> nvtx-range (0.000s)
NVTX: runtime-schedule -> nvtx-range (0.004s)
KERNEL: quant_conv_f16 (starts at +0.012s)
KERNEL: fallback_matmul (starts at +0.016s)
```
aj: can you try toggling explicit kernel selection via env to force fp32/fast-path and re-run capture? e.g., export RFORCE_KERNEL=fastpath_fp32
sara: tried forcing fastpath_fp32, latency improves but CPU spikes persist. suspect batching heuristic + kv cache eviction causing extra host work.
devon: try capturing with sampling disabled and nvtx bracket full flow to get per-kernel durations: ```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none --output=kv-attach-full.qdrep --duration=20 
```
kevin: note: when you do sample=none the qdrep size grows; for quick triage use --capture-range=nvtx to limit. also add --storage=./tmp to avoid /tmp filling up.
perf-bot: alert: past 24h similar regression detected on dedicated-prod for kv-attach path (tag: regression-2026-02). See run 2026-02-14_03 for details. :warning:
sara: thanks perf-bot. plan: 1) narrow down whether the CPU spike is from kv eviction (GC) or scheduling logic, 2) reproduce with minimal batcher (no prefetch) + nsys --sample=cpu to capture host stack.
aj: for host stacks use: ```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --sample=cpu --sample-interval=1ms --output=kv-attach-hoststacks.qdrep --duration=15 
```
devon: if you want kernel timelines and kernel counts per stream, also enable cuda-memcheck? might be heavy. alternatively dump kernel table from qdrep with nsight-ui or `nsys stats` to CSV.
sara: quick checklist I ran: 
- inserted NVTX around batch enqueue, kv-lookup, kv-evict 
- ran nsys with sample=cpu and sample=none variants 
- tried forcing kernel selection envs 
- measured per-batch seq length distribution to ensure seq<32 path is dominating
Observations: with small batches we get more frequent kv-evict calls (~2x) and the runtime decides to preemptively compact cache leading to host work spikes.
kevin: plausible. batching heuristic might be triggering compaction for low occupancy. try increasing batcher aggregation timeout locally (BATCHER_AGG_MS=8 -> 20) and re-run capture. if tail drops then it's a heuristics fix.
sara: will try. one more tip: short-sample captures can miss very short kernels — use bracketed capture with `--capture-range=nvtx:name_start:name_end` and set `--capture-range-end=stop` to ensure you bracket only the critical window.
aj: thanks — also remember to keep device-side sampling flags low overhead; `--sample-interval` granularity matters.
devon: after you're done, export the qdrep and run `nsys stats -f csv -o kv-attach-stats kv-attach.qdrep` and share the kernel table. that helps identify which kernel family spiked.
sara: cool. I'll iterate and drop results here. short-term action: try BATCHER_AGG_MS tweak + nvtx-bracketed nsys with `--sample=cpu` then share stats CSV. :thumbsup:
